title: Evaluation Supply-Chain Governance and Deployment Playbook
author: Priya Suresh
content:
Overview

This playbook describes the ‘evaluation supply chain’ — the full lifecycle and governance needed to author, certify, deploy, and operate evaluation probes and artifacts that verify model quality across Redwood’s hosted, dedicated, and private runtimes. The supply chain concept treats probes, manifests, quant profiles, and shadow traffic adapters as first-class artifacts that must be tracked, versioned, and triaged.

Goals
- Ensure probe artifacts are reproducible and auditable.
- Make eval costs explicit and accountable to owning teams.
- Provide deterministic hedges for quantized and cached execution paths.
- Reduce mean-time-to-resolution (MTTR) for regressions by standardizing triage signals and escalation steps.

Scope
This document covers:
- Probe authoring and ownership (prompt sets, priming templates).
- Eval manifest and artifact registry.
- Deployment gating: shadow -> canary -> staged rollout.
- Quantization compatibility tests and hedging policies.
- Telemetry, alerting, and regression triage runbook.

Principles
1. Treat evaluation assets like code: immutable artifacts (SHA), changelogs, and owners.
2. Keep cost transparency: every scheduled eval run must include a cost estimate and chargeback tag.
3. Fail open for safety-critical checks (safety sentinels), but fail closed for fidelity gates tied to production SLOs.
4. For quantized deployments, require a declared ‘quant-hedge’ (fallback model variant) before rollout.

Roles & Responsibilities| Role | Responsibility | SLA |
| Owner (service/product) | Approves probe families and responds to regression alerts | 48h acknowledgment |
| Eval Steward (applied-ml) | Maintains registry, signs manifests, schedules smoke runs | 24h triage window |
| Runtime Ops | Implements canary routing, enforces hedges at routing layer | 2h during rollouts |
| Annotation Shop | Handles human review re-runs and labeling escalations | Depends on backlog |

Artifact Types and Metadata
- Probe (prompt set): id, version, seed, language, slice-tags, owner, expected-metrics (e.g., exact-match, coherence-score).
- Eval Manifest (YAML): references model version SHA, quant profile id, batch-size budget, telemetry hooks, and rollout policy.
- Quant Profile: name, format (int8/4/mixed), known failure-patterns, required hedges.
- Shadow Adapter: routing config for mirror traffic, sampling ratio, anonymization policy.

Example eval-manifest.yaml (canonical fields)
---
manifest_id: eval-2026-qs-17
probe_id: probe-seq-customer-intent-v2
model_ref: model-suite/seq16/v1.2.3-sha256:abcdef
quant_profile: q-int8-v3
budget: { daily_tokens: 2_000_000, run_quota: 10 }
sampling: { shadow_ratio: 0.02, canary_ratio: 0.01 }
telemetry: [response_time_ms, coherence_score, embedding_stability]
rollback_policy: immediate_on_fidelity_drop
---

Probe Certification Checklist (pre-deploy)
1. Ownership assigned and reviewers listed in manifest.
2. Unit probe coverage >= 95% of known slice taxonomy for the service.
3. Minimal synthetic bias tests run (edgecase, adversarial prompts).
4. Quant-compatibility run completed: delta_coherence <= 2% against float baseline or quant hedges declared.
5. Cost estimate attached to manifest and approved by finance tagger.
6. Shadow adapter configured with PII redaction and rate limits.

Gating and Rollout Patterns
- Shadow Stage (minimum 48 hours): run with shadow_ratio 0.5%–5% dependent on traffic. Monitor fidelity deltas, API error rate, and token-cost leakage.
- Micro-Canary (1%–5% routes): enable circuit breaker for latency tail > 2x baseline.
- Staged Increase: double traffic every 2 hours if no fidelity or latency flags.
- Full Deploy: assert telemetry parity within configured tolerance window (default 24h).

Quantization Hedging Strategy
- For every quant_profile applied to a model, require a hedging descriptor that lists: fallback_model_ref, max_allowed_coherence_delta, and cost_impact_estimate.
- At routing level, implement autopass: if quantized model emits coherence delta > threshold for 5% of recent probes, route new requests to fallback until human review.
- Maintain ‘quant-failure registry’ with annotated failure examples and remediation notes.

Telemetry & Alerting (example thresholds)
- Coherence stability (24h rolling): alert if median delta > 1.5% or 95th percentile delta > 4%.
- Embedding drift score: alert if cluster-shift > 0.12 (cosine drift metric).
- Latency SLO: p99 generation latency > 2x baseline for 10 minutes -> paging to runtime ops.
- Token-cost variance: > 20% increase vs baseline for 6h -> notify owner and finance.

Runbook: Regression Triage (short form)
1. Acknowledge: Eval Steward triages within 1 hour of alert.
2. Snapshot: Freeze the eval-manifest and collect the last 48h of probe outputs, seeds, and model metadata.
3. Reproduce: Run an isolated replay of the probe against (a) float baseline, (b) quantized variant, (c) previous promoted model to local sandbox.
4. Partition: Use slice tags to identify narrow vs broad regressions. If narrow, create targeted repair probe and schedule annotator passes.
5. Blame Assistant: If automated bisect rules identify model-promote as highest-likelihood change, tag as model regression and initiate rollback plan.
6. Rollback or Patch: Execute rollback or a micro-patch canary as defined in manifest. Document RCA and update the quant-failure registry.

Operational Playbook: Emergency rollback steps
1. Set routing override: force 100% traffic to last known-good model.
2. Suspend all ongoing staging rollouts and mark affected manifests as ‘paused’.
3. Notify stakeholders: include owner, runtime ops, applied-ml, and support.
4. Run fast-lane probe battery (10 high-signal probes) to confirm recovery.
5. Postmortem: 72h paper trail and update probes if necessary.

Costing and Chargeback Model
- Every eval job must include a cost center tag. Chargeback is computed as: compute_cost + storage_cost + annotation_cost.
- Priority runs (security/safety) are centrally funded and exempt from chargebacks.
- Monthly eval budget reports are published to the owning team and finance; overspending triggers a review and potential reduction of sampling rates.

Operational Integrations (who and where)
- CI: eval-manifest linting and SHA signing runs inside the eval-harness CI pipeline.
- Artifact Registry: all manifests, probes, and quant profiles are stored in the eval-registry service (artifact://eval-registry/<manifest_id>).
- Observability: telemetry feeds into Redwood Console (per-model dashboards) and a dedicated Eval-Guard Grafana dashboard.
- Incident Management: integrated with PagerDuty rotation for runtime-ops and Eval Steward on-call.

Housekeeping and Tech Debt
- Quarterly sweep: retire probes that have not been referenced by a manifest in 12 months.
- Audit: yearly audit of quant-profiles and hedges for stale entries.
- Debt log: maintain a short-form markdown in the registry: debt items must include owner and target completion quarter.

Appendix A — Example CLI snippets
# Sign a manifest (eval-harness CLI)
redwood-eval sign --manifest eval-manifest.yaml --signer "applied-ml-steward"

# Run a smoke eval locally against a model ref
redwood-eval run --manifest eval-manifest.yaml --model-ref model-suite/seq16/v1.2.3 --local-sandbox

Appendix B — Example failure message and minimum fields for triage ticket
- Summary: Short text describing observed delta.
- Manifest id: eval-2026-qs-17
- Probe ids and seeds: probe-seq-customer-intent-v2 [seed: 54321]
- Observed deltas: coherence +3.6%, latency p99 +120ms, token-cost +12%
- Immediate action taken: routing override to fallback-model-ref
- Attachments: eval logs URL, sample outputs, quant-profile id
